question.text: Tests of market efficiency include all EXCEPT:

explanation.text: The Logic: Tests of the Efficient Market Hypothesis examine whether market prices are predictable from past data or news. Runs tests and autocorrelation tests check randomness in price series (weak-form EMH), while event studies examine how quickly prices adjust to new public information (semi-strong EMH). Portfolio stress tests are scenario-based risk-management exercises that estimate portfolio loss under adverse conditions — they make no statement about market efficiency. The Trap: All three of the first options are standard statistical EMH tests in the academic toolkit. Stress testing answers a different question — tail risk and capital adequacy — not predictability of returns. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers workbook (Sep 2025) discusses stress testing as a portfolio risk-management tool around page 294, but does not enumerate runs tests, autocorrelation tests, or event studies as EMH tests on the cited pages 234-237. The categorisation above is general research-methods knowledge.
